title: The Mirror-Shell Ranks
story: Out on the moonlit salt flats, Sallowdrix the Locust Conductor drills an army of mirror-shell locusts into a perfect marching grid, 14 rows deep and 12 locusts across, all of them clutching stolen seed-grain. Mr 6 clangs his shield against a hollow salt pillar, and the sound sends most of the swarm skittering into the cracks — but exactly three eighths of them hold their ranks. Sallowdrix hurriedly regroups the ones who stayed into 7 equal new rows.
question: How many locusts stand in each of the 7 new rows?
solution: Three eighths hold their ranks: 168 ÷ 8 = 21, and 21 × 3 = 63 locusts remain.
Split into 7 equal rows: 63 ÷ 7 = 9 locusts in each row.
praise: Finding the fraction that stayed was smart thinking — the last step was sharing those leftovers into the 7 new rows.
hint: Three things happen in order: build the grid, keep three eighths of it, then split what's left into 7 rows. Do them one at a time.
victory: Mr 6 counts nine per row and calmly steps into the one gap the tiny formation can't cover. Sallowdrix squeaks, drops the seed-grain, and conducts a very fast retreat across the shining salt.
imagePrompt: Glittering mirror-shelled locusts in neat marching rows across a moonlit white salt flat, a lanky insect conductor waving antennae like a baton, and a small numeral-six knight raising a shield that catches the moonlight.
